items.title: Treasury denies Healey plan to cut welfare bill before election, claiming his comments were misinterpreted – UK politics live
items.summary: Asked earlier if there would be a cut to the welfare bill before the next election, the chancellor said: ‘There will be a reduction in the benefits bill’ Helen Miller , director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies thinktank, is giving a presentation summing up the IFS’s view of the budget. Arguing that it contained plenty of “bad things” as well as welcome measures, she singled out founders’ relief for particular criticism. She said: After years of arguing that business asset disposal relief was a bad idea – and just when I thought the relief was on its last legs – a new, similar relief has popped up. The new founders’ relief looks bonkers. It gives a lower rate of capital gains tax to a small subset of people with large gains. That will include some entrepreneurs that make investments with broader societal benefits – although most of that activity would have happened without the relief.

items.summary: Call it a new Apollo moment: Rocket launches from Cape Canaveral, Florida, are now outpacing those of the Cold War-era space race that first made the launch site famous. Why it matters: U.S. leaders are rushing to grow the number of rocket providers at America's busiest spaceport amid a space and arms race with China. Beijing plans to send a crew to the Moon by 2030 or sooner and is rapidly building up its satellite and rocket fleets. What they're saying: "There's nothing really comparable in the background of my career to what we're experiencing today," Space Force Col. Brian Chatman, the commander of Florida's rocket range, told Axios in an exclusive interview. Behind the scenes: The Cape is busy expanding to meet President Trump's mandate for the nation to support 1,000 annual launches by 2030. Chatman said with all the contractors on base, inspection backups and parking chaos abound.

The crash, between a moving train and another that was stopped further up the track, was caused by an "inexplicable" error, the transport minister said. A high-speed train crash has killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more in central Spain. It occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into another train - which was stationary on the tracks - on Wednesday morning. The force saw several carriages fall down an embankment. The transport minister said a computer failure followed by human error caused the crash, which is one of the worst in Europe's modern history, and Spain's deadliest train disaster in 13 years.

The week, the Windows developer said it would offer buyouts to 60,000 workers as it looks to curb costs. Technology giant Microsoft says its profits for the three months to the end of September jumped to more than $36.6bn (£27.5bn), just days after announcing plans to cut its workforce by more than a quarter. On Monday, the Windows developer said it would offer voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 of its workers to cut costs as it pours billions of dollars into artificial intelligence (AI). Let's look back at the last five Formula 1 winners at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez. Winning a race here is quite the challenge, especially with Mexico City sitting approximately 2,240 meters above sea level. The thin air affects the cars' aerodynamic downforce and drag, making the practice sessions more valuable for the drivers to get used to the changes. Moreover, the run into Turn 1 is relatively longer than most circuits on the calendar, giving drivers plenty of opportunities to overtake. In fact, two of the last five winners of the Mexican GP started from third on the grid.

“CTE is an entirely preventable disease,” Christopher Nowinski, CEO of the Concussion & CTE Foundation, said. A study published Wednesday found that about three in four deceased NFL players from 2008 to 2023 had CTE. According to the study published in JAMA Network Open , researchers examined the donated brains of 396 deceased NFL players who died during that time period and found that about 93.5% had CTE. They also analyzed the death records of 1,966 NFL players in the same time period and found that overall, combined with the donated brains, an estimated 74.5% of them were likely to have the degenerative disease.

A powerful feedback loop could drive more warming than predicted. Climate change itself is increasingly fueling climate change. Rising concentrations of greenhouse gases are driving up global temperatures, setting off dangerous feedback loops that we have not fully accounted for in our climate models—or our emissions-reduction goals. Scientists have long warned that warming would propel further warming in various ways, but a growing number of observations and studies are at last providing a sharper sense of just how powerful these cascading effects could be. And, by extension, they’re showing how much faster the planet may warm in this century.
